entry_conditions: The policy may be entered during the expanded red-place-to-blue-entry corridor when observations are in world metres with known red_pose, blue_pose, red_goal and blue_goal. Supported entries include red already grasped/lifted near indices 130-190, red descending to the red pad around indices 250-300, or the shared transition after red release around index 330 with red_pose near red_goal and the gripper open.
exit_conditions: Exit when red remains at the red pad and the policy has produced a useful blue-entry state: attention/geometry has shifted to blue, TCP is at or above the blue block, and blue has been grasped/lifted. Demonstrated strong exits are near index 520, with blue z about 0.278-0.280 m and fingers closed around 0.018 m per finger. Earlier transfer during blue approach may be reasonable if a successor explicitly handles blue acquisition from an open-gripper TCP-above-blue state.
overlap_role: This policy covers both shared transition phases in the full [130, 520) slice. In the early overlap it continues the red-in-hand lift/carry state from the predecessor. In the long late overlap with blue acquisition it learns red release, upward retreat, travel to blue, gripper closing on blue, and blue lift-entry. The overlap is learned from actions and observations, not implemented as a scripted handoff controller.
successor_readiness: A successor should receive observations showing red_pose close to red_goal [-0.24, -0.25, 0.02], blue selected by the learned/object geometry context, and TCP close to or above blue_pose. For a robust blue-transport successor, prefer blue_pose z substantially above the table and qpos fingers closed; for a blue-acquire successor, an open gripper with TCP descending over blue is still within demonstrated overlap support.
failure_signatures: Potential failures include switching attention to blue before red is at the red pad, reopening or returning to red after release, moving toward blue with the gripper still carrying red, disturbing red while attempting blue pickup, failing to close on blue, or ending with blue still at table height instead of lifted. These are observed-state cues for the inference agent, not hard rejection thresholds inside the model.
continuation_guidance: Continue this policy while red is in hand, while red is descending or being released at the red goal, while TCP retreats upward from the red pad, and while TCP approaches or closes/lifts blue. Causal cues are red_pose-red_goal error, qpos finger opening, TCP-red and TCP-blue offsets, and the two-observation deltas of red, blue and TCP. If red is placed and the gripper is open but TCP is only partway to blue, this policy is still within its trained transition corridor and can keep running toward the blue-entry state.
limitations: The evidence supports the fixed red-then-blue ordering in the training demonstrations only. Grasp/contact is inferred from object motion and finger closure; no tactile signal or explicit grasp detector is available. The handoff document describes observed support and intended selection behavior but does not add IK, collision handling, hard constraints or recovery outside the demonstrated corridor.
